subject: Observability surcharge scenario and technical scope clarifications
messages:
From: Janet Bromley <janet@bromley.ai>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@bromley.ai
Date: 2026-10-04 09:12 -0700
Subject: Clarify observability fees for archive/surge

Hi Sergio —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. The team liked the dashboard UX but procurement needs clarity on the "surge/archival" line in the draft SOW. Two specific asks: 1) how do we get charged if our ingest spikes for two weeks (we have a seasonal audit window), and 2) what happens when we cross the 90-day retention boundary for traces — is that a surcharge or a different bucket?

I'm attaching our projected retention spreadsheet. Can you confirm a simple example (10TB ingest in month 1, 3TB retained beyond 90 days) and what we'd owe? Also: will advanced dashboards incur a seat fee or a metered fee?

Appreciate a short worked example we can pass to procurement.

Best,
Janet
VP Product, Bromley Health

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: Janet Bromley <janet@bromley.ai>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-04 11:03 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify observability fees for archive/surge

Janet —

Quick reply while I pull the model. Short answers up front: 1) short-term ingest spikes are handled by our surge buffer (no immediate surcharge for transient bursts under configured thresholds); 2) traces retained beyond the committed horizon move to the "archive" pricing band which is metered at a lower per-GB rate but with a minimum monthly archival fee if >1TB. Advanced dashboards are licensed per-tenant with an optional per-seat overlay for role-based editor features.

I attached an initial worked example and annotated the SOW with the surge thresholds we used in the demo (surge buffer = 25% of committed ingest for up to 14 days). That should map to your audit window, but want to confirm the typical duration and peak multiple you expect. If Bromley expects repeated seasonal surges we can propose a burst commitment (temporary capacity reservation) or a temporary surcharge cap.

I'll let Kimberly follow up with the concrete numbers/quote.

—Sergio
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Janet Bromley <janet@bromley.ai>, sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-05 08:17 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify observability fees for archive/surge (worked example attached)

Janet —

Thanks for the spreadsheet. I ran a conservative worked example and pasted the simplified math below so procurement can see line items. Full calc in the attached retention-cost-model.xlsx.

Scenario (month 1 ingest = 10TB, month 2 steady ingest = 4TB, 3TB retained beyond 90 days):
- Ingest metering (month 1): 10TB @ $0.10/GB = $1,024* (one-time ingest processing)
- Surge buffer: first 25% of spikes covered — no surcharge for up to 2.5TB of the 10TB spike
- Archive (beyond 90d): 3TB @ $0.015/GB/month = $46/month
- Archive minimum monthly fee: $500 if archive >1TB (applies here) — we bill the higher of per-GB or min fee
- Advanced dashboards: platform license $1,200/month + $15/editor-seat/month (you currently have 8 editors)

Net for month 2 onward (steady state with 3TB archived): $1,200 + (8*$15) + $500 = $1,920/month + small per-GB archival adjustment if usage grows.

Concessions we can offer for an initial 6-month period: waive the archive minimum fee for months 1-3 and provide a 15% discount on advanced-dashboard platform fee for months 1-6. That reduces the onboarding friction for you while we validate retention patterns.

Two technical scope clarifications before I finalize the formal quote:
1) Do you need trace-level indexing beyond 180 days for search (that increases index storage costs)?
2) Will you use sampling rules from the agent or server side? If agent-side low-sample-ingest is viable, it materially reduces long-term archive.

If both are "no," I can lock the proposed concession into the quote and get legal to prep the SOW changes.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Solutions Pricing, Redwood Inference

From: Janet Bromley <janet@bromley.ai>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@bromley.ai
Date: 2026-10-06 09:46 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify observability fees for archive/surge (worked example attached)

Kim, Sergio —

Thanks, that math is helpful and the concession looks reasonable. Quick answers:
- We do not plan to keep trace-level indexes beyond 120 days except for flagged audit traces. So default is no long-term index.
- Sampling will be agent-side for 95% of traffic; flagged routes will be full-fidelity.

Couple of asks from procurement before we sign: 1) can you formalize the "waive archive minimum for months 1-3" language in the SOW and 2) add a one-time onboarding credit equivalent to one month of the advanced dashboards platform fee (to help offset integration costs).

Can you also confirm the maximum surcharge cap if we exceed surge buffer for >14 days (procurement prefers a predictable cap).

Janet
VP Product, Bromley Health

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Janet Bromley <janet@bromley.ai>, sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-07 16:02 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify observability fees for archive/surge (worked example attached)

Janet —

Great — thanks for the quick clarifications. We'll do the following and circulate an updated SOW by tomorrow:

1) SOW language: explicitly waive archive minimum fee for months 1–3; after month 3, archive billing follows the standard banding (per-GB or min $500/month).
2) One-time onboarding credit: apply credit equal to one month of the advanced dashboards platform fee ($1,200) to your first invoice.
3) Surge cap: if you exceed the 25% surge buffer for more than 14 consecutive days, surcharge is computed as 50% of the standard ingest processing rate for the overage, capped at $12,000/month (this cap can be re-negotiated for multi-year commits).

Action items: Jordan, can you run the formal quote lines (with concession flags) and attach the revised SOW and the billing appendix?

Janet — once Jordan uploads, I'll route through legal for a quick review. If this looks good I'll also add the concession terms into the HubSpot deal notes (BRM-4387).

Thanks —
Kimberly
Head of Solutions Pricing, Redwood Inference
